propositions: The epic's headline acceptance criterion requires bidirectional data flow proven live: a DC-created issue must appear in the local store after an inbound pass, and a local edit must appear on the DC issue after an outbound pass, both against a realistic store copy not an empty instance.

The store copy must be isolated from production by constructing it in a fresh git repo with no remote configured, scrubbing all .bridge_state* artifacts and bindings that reference production Jira keys, and asserting both isolation layers hold before any mutation is applied.

The comprehensive mutation suite requires 28 cells (14 inbound and 14 outbound) plus pagination and idempotence, each asserting an individual round-trip oracle against a named observable path on the local or DC side, never relying on aggregate 'converged' signals that mask partial failures.

Four product defects were discovered and isolated by the test suite: phantom outbound updates after convergence due to snapshot differ field drift; DC transport missing status-field-to-transition routing that Cloud transport has; inbound link skips due to phase ordering when targets are unbound; and DC snapshot-absent keys incorrectly planned as outbound creates.

The existing test infrastructure was buggy in ways that masked product defects: idempotence and round-trip assertions bundled into one cell conflated thirteen false reds with real findings; a filter-match implementation that could not match inbound creates by target key; and an assignee oracle that compared ensure_identity_for against itself.
